items.title: Nabis June 2026 California and New York Cannabis Policy Updates
items.summary: California and New York are tightening cannabis regulations in June 2026 across packaging, labeling, and supply chain compliance. In California, AB 2532 caps cannabis beverage servings at 10 mg THC and requires the national Poison Help line on all edible and beverage labels, likely taking effect July 1, 2027. AB 2249 bans cannabis packaging attractive to children — including cartoons, anthropomorphic characters, and certain font styles — and requires the Department of Cannabis Control to publish a compliance rubric by July 1, 2027, with sales allowed through January 1, 2028. In New York, lawmakers passed A10698, the Cannabis Supply Chain Integrity and Anti-Inversion Act, on June 2, 2026, defining and penalizing "cannabis inversion" — the introduction of illicit cannabis into the licensed supply chain — with civil penalties up to $10,000 per day and a rebuttable presumption of license revocation for labs that submit fraudulent certificates of analysis. Separately, California's SB 54 required cannabis operators to register with CalRecycle as a Producer by June 1, 2026, ahead of a 2032 deadline for recyclable or compostable packaging. Here's what licensed operators need to know about each bill and what to do now.
